headline: On OPT? Look for *7.65%* on your pay stub

items.title: Find the two lines

ig_caption:
On OPT or a campus job? Check your pay stub for Social Security and Medicare. Together that's 7.65% of your pay, about $1,530 on $20,000 of wages.

✔️ F-1, J-1 and M-1 students who are nonresidents for tax (generally under 5 calendar years in the US) usually don't owe these on permitted work like OPT.
✔️ Ask your payroll team first to stop it and pay it back.
✔️ If they won't, you can claim it from the IRS on Form 843 with Form 8316.

This doesn't cover F-2 or J-2 family members, H-1B pay, or students who have become residents for tax. We can prepare the full claim for you.

Comment FICA and we'll send you the link, or find it at mfa-advisory.com/international-students

General information, not tax advice.

li_caption:
Many F-1 students on OPT have Social Security and Medicare taken from their pay when they don't owe it. That's 7.65% of wages, or about $1,530 on $20,000.

How to check and fix it:

1. Read the pay stub. Look for Social Security (6.2%) and Medicare (1.45%), often labeled OASDI and MED.
2. Check the status. The IRS says F-1, J-1 and M-1 students who are nonresident aliens (generally fewer than 5 calendar years in the US) are exempt on wages for permitted work, including practical training on or off campus.
3. Ask the employer first. Payroll can stop the withholding and refund what was taken.
4. If the employer won't refund it all, file Form 843 with the IRS, with Form 8316, the W-2, the passport visa page and the I-94.

The exemption doesn't cover F-2, J-2 or M-2 family members, H-1B wages, or students who have become residents for tax.

We prepare the Form 843 claim with Form 8316 and the document checklist for you. Comment FICA and we will send it, or see https://mfa-advisory.com/international-students/?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=nov-push

sources.fact: Nonresident alien students in F-1, J-1 or M-1 status (less than 5 calendar years) are generally exempt from Social Security and Medicare on wages for USCIS-allowed work, including practical training on or off campus; not for F-2/J-2/M-2, other non-exempt statuses, or students who become resident aliens; ask the employer first, then Form 843 with Form 8316
Form 843 attachments: W-2, passport page with visa, I-94, I-538 if applicable, employer statement (or your own), Form 8316
Form 8316: first try to get the refund from your employer
Employee rates: Social Security 6.2%, Medicare 1.45% (7.65% total); $20,000 x 7.65% = $1,530
